raw_response:
I’m 63 now, so I don’t chase fancy changes just because someone says they’re new. On 35 mu, with only two people in the house, I need a plan that is steady, not too labor-heavy, and still brings cash flow. I’ll keep most of the land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the most reliable system here, and I’ll leave part in cotton for diversification and cash income. Since I have well irrigation, I can protect wheat at the key spring stages and help maize if the summer rain is short. With my experience, I’d rather stay near the upper-middle input range than cut too much and risk yield loss, but I still watch costs carefully because pumping water, fertilizer, and hired machine work all add up.

For the wheat already in the field, my focus this spring is jointing to grain filling: one main topdress of nitrogen, then 2 to 3 irrigations depending on rainfall, and disease control only if I actually see pressure. After harvest in June, I’ll turn those same fields quickly into summer maize with minimum delay, because in Quzhou the wheat-maize window is tight. Cotton goes on the separate land in late April; I’ll use a cleaner seed lot, moderate plant density, and split fertilizer because cotton responds better when I don’t dump it all at once. With only two household members, I will rely on machinery or custom service for wheat harvest, maize sowing, and some spraying, and keep hand labor mostly for cotton management.
